title: Deep learning estimates HbA1c from the electrocardiogram in a retrospective cohort
summary: A deep learning model was trained on 104,823 ECGs to estimate HbA1c. In a follow-up cohort it reached an AUC of 0.8255 (sensitivity 71.9%, specificity 77.7%) for distinguishing diabetes, and higher ECG-HbA1c was linked to future mortality, new chronic kidney disease and new heart failure. The study is retrospective at a single health system with modest discrimination.
ai_technology: Deep learning model estimating HbA1c from ECG
organization: Division of Cardiology, Department of Internal Medicine, Tri-Service General Hospital, National Defense Medical Center, Taipei, Taiwan

evidence.tested: Validation in 1539 cases (2190 ECGs) and a 3293-case follow-up cohort for diabetes detection and complication prediction.
evidence.unknown: Prospective or multi-system performance and any effect on diabetes management; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model converted ECG signals into an HbA1c estimate used for detection and risk prediction.
